fields.meta_title: Landing Page SEO: Build One Page per Query | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Landing page SEO in seven steps, with launch checks from Google's own tools and a builder that hands you the page as code. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Landing Page SEO Into Code You Own, Tag by Tag
fields.hero_description: Describe the offer and the query it should answer. Emergent builds the page and its lead form as code you own, with the title tag and schema you specify.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into an SEO Landing Page
fields.features_subheading: The parts of landing page SEO Emergent writes into the page from your prompt, and where its leads are saved.
fields.feature_1:
Meta tags written around the query

Your prompt names the query, and Emergent writes the page's title and description tags around it. Rewording either one later takes a follow-up message that edits the code.
fields.feature_2:
Sections in the order searchers need them

Emergent lays out the H2s around the questions your buyers ask next, in the order you list them. The lead form goes where you place it: under the opening section or at the end.
fields.feature_3:
Structured data and canonical tags

Structured data goes in as JSON-LD, the format Google recommends, for whichever schema.org type your prompt names. A canonical URL and a sitemap entry go in on request too.
fields.feature_4:
Speed findings you can fix by prompt

PageSpeed Insights reports Core Web Vitals for the published page. Paste a finding, such as an image served larger than it displays, into the chat and Emergent fixes the code.
fields.feature_5:
Leads saved with their landing URL

Submissions land in a database you own, tagged with the landing URL and referrer you ask the form to record. Filter on the referrer to split organic leads from paid ones.
fields.feature_6:
Markup you can audit and keep

Export the page, form included, to your GitHub repository as plain code. Your developer can then check every tag, JSON-LD included, with whichever crawler they already use.

fields.usecase_heading: SEO Landing Pages for Four Kinds of Query
fields.tab_content_1:
One feature page for one buying query

Northwind sells shift scheduling software, and that phrase is what its buyers search. The prompt puts it in the title tag, H1 and URL, with SoftwareApplication markup for the product. Demo requests land in a table with the landing URL attached.
fields.tab_content_2:
Four branches with copy of their own

A moving company has crews in four Colorado cities, and they do different work. Downtown high-rises lead the Denver page; Boulder's is about student moves. LocalBusiness markup on every page carries the branch address. Quote requests post to the Slack channel of the branch they came from.
fields.tab_content_3:
What a fair comparison table shows

A rival's strengths stay in the table. The Acme vs Globex page keeps the mobile app row, where Globex is ahead. BreadcrumbList markup places the page under Compare, and the feature pages it mentions are linked from the bottom.
fields.tab_content_4:
The template preview comes before the email field

Nothing is gated until the visitor has seen the content calendar template: a preview of the sheet and short notes on filling it in. Maya at Lumen enters her work email and the file downloads. Her new HubSpot contact lists this page as the source.

fields.howto_title: How to Build an SEO Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Start from one query and the pages already ranking for it. Build the page to that standard, then judge it by the leads it brings in, not by traffic alone.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Match what the top results deliver
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Answer before you ask for anything
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose the single query the page should rank for and check that the top results are pages like yours. If the first page of Google is all guides, write a guide-shaped page or pick another query.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the top ten and note what they have in common: format, length, whether they show prices, which questions their H2s cover. Match the format, then answer what they skip, such as setup time when every result stops at features.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write a concise title tag that names the query and differs from every other title on the site. The meta description should summarize this page alone, though Google may show text from the page instead.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Answer the query in the opening section, in plain words. Cover the topic at the depth the top results set, and place the form after that answer. Ask only for the fields you will use, and say what happens after someone submits.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Mark up the page with the schema.org type that matches it, and include every property Google lists as required for that type. Then link to the new page from related pages, with anchor text that names its topic.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test the page on a phone
fields.howto_step_6_des: Load the page on a mid-range phone before launch. Give every image a width and height attribute and the layout holds still while it loads. Any script in the head that the first screen does not need should carry async or defer.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the page on your own domain. Once a week, set its clicks from search beside the leads in your database. When clicks rise and leads do not, test the offer and the form before rewriting the copy for search.

findings.quote: Submissions land in a database you own, tagged with the landing URL and referrer you ask the form to record. Filter on the referrer to split organic leads from paid ones.
findings.issue: Wrong about how referrers work and no domain_sources entry: a Google Ads click and an organic Google click both arrive with a google.com referrer, so the referrer cannot split paid search from organic search, the very split a landing page SEO reader cares about (FAQ 4 sends paid clicks to a PPC page). Paid traffic is told apart by UTM tags or the gclid auto-tagging parameter. No other field repeats the claim (checked tab_content_1, howto_step_7_des, faq).
findings.fix: Record the URL's UTM tags instead, e.g. 'tagged with the landing URL and the UTM tags you ask the form to record. Filter on utm_medium to split organic leads from paid ones.' Then add a source for the UTM or auto-tagging line to domain_sources (Google Ads help on auto-tagging).

findings.quote: They can, as long as each landing page targets a query no other page on the site covers. When pages are near duplicates, Google picks one as canonical, and its results usually point to that page.
findings.issue: Overstated SEO advice, the same class as the cycle-4 findings: 'as long as' makes one query per page a condition for landing pages helping SEO, and the cited source (Google's canonicalization doc) covers duplicate content, not two pages that target the same query. Pages can share a query without being near duplicates, so the second sentence does not support the first.
findings.fix: Keep to the source: 'They can, when each page carries content of its own. Google clusters near-duplicate pages, picks one as canonical, and its results usually point to that page.' Or source the one-query-per-page advice and drop 'as long as'.

findings.quote: The parts of landing page SEO Emergent writes into the page from your prompt, and where its leads are saved.
findings.issue: The SERP carries an AI Overview; the rule asks for a one or two sentence definition of the primary in the hero or features subheading as well as FAQ 1. Neither field defines landing page SEO (the approved thank-you page set a lax precedent, so a note).
findings.fix: Open the subheading with the sourced definition: 'Landing page SEO is building a page to rank for one query and turn its visitors into leads. Here is what Emergent writes into it.'

findings.quote: 'If the first page of Google is all guides, write a guide-shaped page or pick another query.'; 'Match the format, then answer what they skip'; 'place the form after that answer. Ask only for the fields you will use'; 'test the offer and the form before rewriting the copy for search'
findings.issue: Best-practice advice with no domain_sources entry. Stated as method, not as fact about Google, so lower risk; step 1 still implies how Google ranks.
findings.fix: Add a source for search-intent matching (Semrush's SEO landing page guide, already in domain_sources, covers it) and for form length, or soften step 1 to the check itself.

findings.quote: Give every image a width and height attribute and the layout holds still while it loads.
findings.issue: Goes beyond web.dev: the attributes reserve image space and prevent that shift; fonts, embeds and injected content can still move the layout.
findings.fix: '...and the browser reserves each image's space before it loads.'

findings.quote: PageSpeed Insights reports Core Web Vitals for the published page.
findings.issue: Field Core Web Vitals appear only once a URL has enough Chrome UX Report traffic; a new landing page gets lab data (LCP, CLS, no INP).
findings.fix: 'PageSpeed Insights runs a lab test on the published page' or 'reports speed findings for the published page'.

findings.quote: 'Close a landing page SEO checklist with three checks before launch. ... Then use URL Inspection in Search Console'; 'Its Performance report lists the queries each page appears for'
findings.issue: URL Inspection's live test needs the URL reachable on the internet in a verified property, so it runs at launch, not before it. The Performance report leaves out anonymized queries, so it does not list every query.
findings.fix: 'three checks on launch day'; 'lists the queries each page appears for' -> 'lists the top queries each page appears for'.

findings.quote: Close a landing page SEO checklist with three checks before launch.
findings.issue: The question asks what belongs on the checklist; the first sentence answers only how it ends.
findings.fix: Answer first: 'The seven steps above are the checklist; close it with three launch checks.'

findings.quote: For a single storefront or office, start with a local business landing page.
findings.issue: A local business page is not one of the four types just named; the link sentence reads as a non sequitur (same class as the cycle-4 note on this item).
findings.fix: Tie it to a type: 'A lead capture page suits a single storefront or office; see local business landing page.'

review_notes.issue: The SERP carries an AI Overview; the rule asks for a one or two sentence definition of the primary in the hero or features subheading as well as FAQ 1. Neither field defines landing page SEO (the approved thank-you page set a lax precedent, so a note).
review_notes.fix: Open the subheading with the sourced definition: 'Landing page SEO is building a page to rank for one query and turn its visitors into leads. Here is what Emergent writes into it.'

review_notes.issue: Best-practice advice with no domain_sources entry. Stated as method, not as fact about Google, so lower risk; step 1 still implies how Google ranks.
review_notes.fix: Add a source for search-intent matching (Semrush's SEO landing page guide, already in domain_sources, covers it) and for form length, or soften step 1 to the check itself.

review_notes.issue: Goes beyond web.dev: the attributes reserve image space and prevent that shift; fonts, embeds and injected content can still move the layout.
review_notes.fix: '...and the browser reserves each image's space before it loads.'

review_notes.issue: Field Core Web Vitals appear only once a URL has enough Chrome UX Report traffic; a new landing page gets lab data (LCP, CLS, no INP).
review_notes.fix: 'PageSpeed Insights runs a lab test on the published page' or 'reports speed findings for the published page'.

review_notes.issue: URL Inspection's live test needs the URL reachable on the internet in a verified property, so it runs at launch, not before it. The Performance report leaves out anonymized queries, so it does not list every query.
review_notes.fix: 'three checks on launch day'; 'lists the queries each page appears for' -> 'lists the top queries each page appears for'.

review_notes.issue: The question asks what belongs on the checklist; the first sentence answers only how it ends.
review_notes.fix: Answer first: 'The seven steps above are the checklist; close it with three launch checks.'

review_notes.issue: A local business page is not one of the four types just named; the link sentence reads as a non sequitur (same class as the cycle-4 note on this item).
review_notes.fix: Tie it to a type: 'A lead capture page suits a single storefront or office; see local business landing page.'

review_notes.field: feature_3, faq items 4, 5, 9; feature_3, howto_step_5_des, faq item 5; faq item 2, howto_step_7_des
review_notes.issue: Canonical tags, schema and Search Console each recur across 3-4 fields.
review_notes.fix: Let each idea do its work once; other fields add what is new.

review_notes.issue: The drawn table adds an Integrations row the mockup prompt ('Compare pricing, setup time and the mobile app') does not ask for, and the table does not mention the scheduling, reporting and payroll pages the label says it mentions.
review_notes.fix: Drop the Integrations row or add it to the prompt; label the chips 'Related feature pages'.

review_notes.issue: QC K7: Wix is not in this page's top 10 (pending with Divit); it is the PAA brand.
review_notes.fix: Divit's ruling on K7.

review_notes.issue: Links to pages not yet live; publish gate holds this page (pending with Divit).
review_notes.fix: Publish with or after those pages.
